newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TRINIDAD RETAINS IBF WELTERWEIGHT CROWN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TRINIDAD RETAINS IBF WELTERWEIGHT CROWN.

text.p: Felix Trinidad of Puerto Rico retained his International Boxing Federation (IBF) welterweight championship by stopping American Ray Lovato in the sixth round on Saturday.

Trinidad, 23, staggered Lovato with a hard right-left combination. Moments later Trinidad landed a left hand to the head as Lovata was coming in and another left to the body followed by a right that staggered Lovato.

The final series was a left-right combination to the head that sent Lovato into the ropes, bringing referee Mitch Helpern in to stop the scheduled 12-round fight at one minute, 57 seconds of the round.
The first two rounds brought scattered boos from the crowd at the MGM Grand Arena as the two fighters mostly danced around each other.

Trinidad began to find the range in the second round and by the third round, with Lovato carrying his left hand low, there were red splotches on Lovato's face and a small cut along the side of his nose.
Trinidad, now 30-0, won the 147-pound (66.6 kg) IBF title in his first world championship bout in June 1993, when he knocked out Maurice Blocker in the second round.
Trinidad has successfully defended his title 10 times.
